source=json.loads(Path('/spec/formal-context.json').read_text())
result={
 'schema_version':1,
 'candidate_hash':source['candidate_hash'],
 'status':'complete',
 'statement':'For every real relative-error rounding model (u, r) with u >= 0 and, for each real z, some real delta satisfying |delta| <= u and r(z) = z(1 + delta), every finite list c of real coefficients, and every real x, the recursively rounded evaluation Q(model,c,x) differs from the exact evaluation P(c,x) by at most E(c,x,u): |Q(model,c,x) - P(c,x)| <= E(c,x,u). The constructions P, Q, and E are the list recursions specified below; the bound uses the exact tail evaluation P in its local terms.',
 'targets':[
  {'name':'Research.Horner.forward_error','statement':'For all model : Research.FloatingPoint.Model, all finite lists coefficients of real numbers, and all x in R, |Q(model,coefficients,x) - P(coefficients,x)| <= E(coefficients,x,model.u). Here a model consists of a real u >= 0 and a function r : R -> R such that for every z in R there exists delta in R with |delta| <= u and r(z) = z(1 + delta); r = model.round and u = model.u. P, Q, and E are exactly the constructions below. Thus this is an absolute forward-error bound for the specified computation Q relative to P, for arbitrary list length and real evaluation point. There is no additional hypothesis on the coefficients, x, or the size of u.'}
 ],
 'constructions':[
  {'name':'Research.Horner.P','description':'P : List(R) x R -> R. For every real x, P([],x) = 0. For every real a and finite real list t, P(a::t,x) = a + x P(t,x). Consequently for c = [a_0,...,a_(n-1)], P(c,x) is the sum over integers i with 0 <= i < n of a_i x"'^i, with empty sum 0. The first list entry is the constant coefficient. All these operations are exact real operations.'"'},
  {'name':'Research.Horner.Q','description':'Q : Research.FloatingPoint.Model x List(R) x R -> R. For a model with rounding function r and every real x, Q(model,[],x) = 0. For every real a and finite real list t, Q(model,a::t,x) = r(a + r(x Q(model,t,x))). It recursively evaluates the tail using the same model and x, rounds the product of x and that computed tail, adds a exactly, and rounds that sum. Each nonempty-list step applies r twice, including the last coefficient step with tail value 0; there is no special case returning the last coefficient directly. The inputs a and x are not separately rounded. This is the actual computation whose error is bounded by the target theorem.'},
  {'name':'Research.Horner.E','description':'E : List(R) x R x R -> R, defined for every finite real list and all real x and u, even when u < 0. E([],x,u) = 0. For a real a and finite real list t, set v = P(t,x) and e = E(t,x,u); then E(a::t,x,u) = u |a + x v| + (1 + u)(u |x v| + (1 + u)|x| e). In particular v is the exact tail evaluation, not Q. This recursively defined real quantity is used by the theorem as an upper bound after substituting the nonnegative model parameter u = model.u. Its definition itself imposes no restrictions on x or u.'}
 ],
 'assumptions':[
  'A rounding model supplies u in R with 0 <= u and a total function r : R -> R satisfying: for every z in R there exists delta in R such that |delta| <= u and r(z) = z(1 + delta). The existential delta may depend on z; no single common delta is required.',
  'The same model and rounding function are used throughout Q. No particular floating-point format, discretization, tie rule, or bound u < 1 is assumed by the supplied model.',
  'Coefficients are arbitrary finite lists of real numbers, including the empty list, and x is any real number. There are no sign, nonzero-leading-coefficient, degree, length, or magnitude restrictions.',
  'All arithmetic and absolute values in the definitions and theorem are over the real numbers; only the explicit applications of model.round in Q perform rounding. E uses the model parameter only when instantiated in the theorem.'
 ],
 'missing_context':[]
}
assert [x['name'] for x in result['targets']]==source['targets']
assert [x['name'] for x in result['constructions']]==source['construction_names']
assert set(result)=={'schema_version','candidate_hash','status','statement','targets','constructions','assumptions','missing_context'}
os.makedirs('/output',exist_ok=True)
fd,tmp=tempfile.mkstemp(prefix='.translation-',suffix='.json',dir='/output')
try:
 with os.fdopen(fd,'w') as f:
  json.dump(result,f,ensure_ascii=False,indent=2)
  f.write('\\n')
  f.flush()
  os.fsync(f.fileno())
 os.replace(tmp,'/output/translation.json')
finally:
 if os.path.exists(tmp): os.unlink(tmp)
print('Saved /output/translation.json; status=complete; 1 target; 3 constructions.')
PY"
